best_facts.fact: In 1916 and 1917 Thomas Cobden-Sanderson threw his entire Doves Type off Hammersmith Bridge so that his estranged partner could never use it. About 150 pieces were fished out of the Thames in 2014.
best_facts.why_surprising: A typeface was the subject of a revenge drowning.

best_facts.fact: A 2001 study estimated that the layout of the butterfly ballot in Palm Beach County led more than 2,000 Gore voters to vote for Pat Buchanan by mistake. Bush won Florida by 537 votes.
best_facts.why_surprising: A layout choice may have decided a presidency.

best_facts.fact: Comic Sans exists because the cartoon dog in Microsoft Bob was speaking in Times New Roman, which its designer Vincent Connare thought ridiculous.
best_facts.why_surprising: The world's most mocked font began as a fix for a joke.

best_facts.fact: A trust deed in Pakistan's Panama Papers case was dated 2006 but typed in Calibri, which Microsoft did not release commercially until 2007.
best_facts.why_surprising: A font acted like a timestamp in a corruption probe.

best_facts.fact: The only typeface on the Moon is Futura, on the plaque Apollo 11 left in July 1969.
best_facts.why_surprising: A 1927 German typeface is the human signature on another world.

best_facts.fact: Lorem ipsum is not gibberish. It is a scrambled passage from Cicero's De finibus, 45 BCE, about pain: dolorem ipsum lost its first letters.
The girl in Britain's school crossing road sign is based on a photograph of its designer, Margaret Calvert, as a child.
best_facts.why_surprising: A national road sign contains a self-portrait.

best_facts.fact: Jikji, the world's oldest surviving book printed with movable metal type (Korea, 1377), is in Paris, at the Bibliothèque nationale de France.
best_facts.why_surprising: Metal type predates Gutenberg in Asia, and the proof is in France.

best_facts.fact: Hangul's consonant shapes are drawings of the mouth: the letter for k shows the tongue touching the back of the mouth.
best_facts.why_surprising: An alphabet designed as phonetic diagrams.

best_facts.fact: In a 2012 New York Times reader test of about 45,000 people, the same passage was most believed in Baskerville and least in Comic Sans.
best_facts.why_surprising: The clothes of words nudged belief.

best_facts.fact: Lin Yutang's lost 1947 Chinese typewriter, the MingKwai, turned up in a New York basement in 2025. Its pick-from-candidates idea is how most people type Chinese on phones.
best_facts.why_surprising: A lost prototype predicted modern input methods.

best_facts.fact: Sans Forgetica, a font designed to boost memory by being hard to read, showed no memory benefit in three preregistered experiments in 2020.
best_facts.why_surprising: A worldwide headline did not survive testing.

best_facts.fact: Linotype operators sometimes left the nonsense phrase etaoin shrdlu in newspapers: it is what you get running a finger down the first two columns of the keyboard.
best_facts.why_surprising: Typos had a fingerprint in hot metal.

best_facts.fact: Several fonts sold as Garamond in the 20th century were actually based on Jean Jannon's types from about 80 years later. Beatrice Warde exposed the mix-up in 1926 under a male pen name.
best_facts.why_surprising: The classic book face was misattributed for decades.

best_facts.fact: Google's Noto font family takes its name from 'no more tofu', the empty boxes shown for characters a font cannot display.
best_facts.why_surprising: A global typeface project is named after a joke about bean curd.

best_facts.fact: The US State Department changed its official typeface twice in under three years: Times New Roman to Calibri in January 2023, and back in December 2025.
Tolong Siki, a script created in Jharkhand by Dr Narayan Oraon for the Kurukh language, was added to Unicode in September 2025.
best_facts.why_surprising: A writing system from an Indian district now sits in the global standard.

best_facts.fact: Italic type was invented in 1501 to squeeze classics into small, cheap books, not to add emphasis.
best_facts.why_surprising: Emphasis was a later job for italics.

side_dish.title: Why a hard-to-read font makes you trust a claim less
side_dish.body_md:
Psychologists call it processing fluency: the ease with which the mind handles information. When something is easy to read, hear or picture, people tend to judge it as more true, more familiar and more likeable, without noticing why. In classic experiments, statements printed in high-contrast, clear type were rated true more often than the same statements in faint or awkward type. Rhyming sayings are judged more accurate than plain ones that say the same thing. Company names that are easy to pronounce have even been linked to better early trading on stock markets.

This is why Errol Morris's Baskerville result is plausible, and why Sans Forgetica's idea was not crazy: if disfluency makes people slow down, maybe they think harder. The trouble is that fluency effects are often small and depend on context. A 2015 project replicating the claim that hard-to-read fonts improve reasoning on tricky questions found the effect largely disappeared in large samples.

For a designer, the practical lesson is simple. Clarity is not only courtesy. It changes how much your reader believes you. A clear typeface, good contrast and plain words make your message feel more credible, which is a power worth using honestly.

offline_task.title: A typography walk
offline_task.body_md: Take a 20 minute walk, or go through your kitchen and bag, and collect five examples of type doing a job. Find one sign meant to be read at a distance (a road sign, shop board or station name): is it mixed case or all capitals, and could you read it from far away? Find one piece of hand-painted lettering. Find a product label where the type sets a mood: luxury, cheap, healthy, playful. Find one place where two or more scripts sit together, such as Hindi and English, and see whether they look like a matched pair or strangers. Finally, find one example of bad typography and say exactly what is wrong: line length, spacing, contrast, size or tone. Photograph each and write one sentence about what the type is for.
